avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction reduces nateglinide plasma concentrations and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, monitor blood glucose closely and adjust nateglinide dose

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate hypoglycemic effects and increase insulin secretion independently
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use with caution; monitor blood glucose and educate patient on hypoglycemia signs

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have additive glucose-lowering effects; limited evidence but potential for enhanced hypoglycemia
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; counsel patient on hypoglycemia awareness and monitor glucose trends

caution_supplements.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance insulin secretion and glucose utilization; additive hypoglycemic potential
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood glucose regularly; inform patient of hypoglycemia risk with concurrent use

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: Delays nateglinide absorption and peak plasma concentrations; reduces glucose control at critical meal times
avoid_foods.action: Take nateglinide 1-30 minutes before meals; counsel patient to avoid high-fat foods with meals for optimal efficacy

caution_foods.name: Alcohol (moderate-to-heavy consumption)
caution_foods.mechanism: Alcohol may enhance and prolong hypoglycemic effects by impairing hepatic glucose production
caution_foods.action: Advise limited alcohol intake; educate on hypoglycemia risk and carry fast-acting carbohydrates when drinking

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may increase nateglinide levels; clinical significance unclear but potential for enhanced effect
caution_foods.action: Limit grapefruit juice consumption; monitor for signs of hypoglycemia if intake unavoidable

monitoring_notes: Monitor fasting and postprandial blood glucose regularly, especially when starting therapy or adding interacting supplements. Assess for hypoglycemic episodes and adjust nateglinide dosing based on glycemic response; counsel patients that nateglinide must be taken shortly before meals for optimal efficacy.
